definitions.interspinales cervicalis muscle: A muscle of the vertebral column consisting of short paired fascicles that span between the spinous processes of contiguous cervical vertebrae (typically C2 through T1), lying on either side of the interspinous ligament. It assists in extension of the cervical spine and contributes to segmental stabilisation and proprioception of the neck.

name_corrections.reason: TA2 / standard anatomical nomenclature uses 'musculi interspinales cervicis' (genitive 'cervicis', not 'cervicalis'). 'Cervicalis' is grammatically the adjective form, but the established TA term is 'interspinales cervicis'. Keep 'interspinales cervicalis muscle' as a related synonym.
